correctness.rationale: A≠singular in GL2(Fq) defines projective fixed lines of [v]↦[Av^{[2]}]; each fixed line lifts to one nonzero idempotent, so N is the number of rational roots of a nonzero cubic (N≤3). PGL2(Fq) is sharply 3-transitive on ordered triples of distinct P1 points; a k-tuple of fixed points is feasible iff coordinatewise squaring yields distinct images. For even q, squaring is bijective and T1,T2,T3=(q+1,(q+1)q,(q+1)q(q−1)); for odd q, fiber collisions yield T2=q²+1 and T3=(q−1)(q²−2q+3). Exact factorial-moment inversion gives the claimed 4-value distribution, including P0=1/3 in both characteristics, zero P2 in even characteristic. Independent prime-field matrix/projective-root enumeration q=3,5,7,11 and direct raw vector-idempotent enumeration q=2,3,5,7 agree. Proof handles all finite extension fields and q=2; finite samples do not stand in for it.

value.rationale: This is the complete natural law of rational idempotent counts in the first nontrivial random perfect evolution-algebra dimension, quantifying the chance of idempotent-free structures beyond existence and mean one. Exact characteristic-two S3 fixed-point law and odd-characteristic correction distinguish arithmetic regimes and supply explicit data for the survey's asymptotic conjecture. No paper-sized future application is needed for this self-contained invariant.
